questions.q: How is a prepayment entered in Oracle Fusion Payables?
options: As a note attached to a future standard invoice
As its own distinct invoice type, separate from a Standard invoice
As a line item on a purchase order
It cannot be entered -- it must be handled outside the system
questions.explain: A prepayment is created and processed as its own invoice type, with its own distribution and payment.

questions.q: What is the difference between a Temporary and a Permanent prepayment?
options: There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
A Temporary prepayment expires after 30 days; a Permanent one never does
A Temporary prepayment is intended to be applied to a future standard invoice; a Permanent one is not
A Permanent prepayment can only be used for capital purchases
questions.explain: Temporary prepayments are designed to offset a later standard invoice; permanent prepayments are not applied to anything afterward.

questions.q: What must be true about a prepayment before it can be applied to a standard invoice?
options: It must be fully paid and have an unapplied amount remaining
It must be for a different supplier than the standard invoice
It must be created after the standard invoice
questions.explain: Only a fully paid prepayment with remaining unapplied amount, for the same supplier, is eligible to be applied.

questions.q: In the BrightPath Consulting Group example, a $6,000 prepayment is applied against a $20,000 standard invoice. What is the net amount still payable?
questions.explain: $20,000 minus the $6,000 already-paid prepayment leaves $14,000 still owed.

questions.q: What risk does applying a prepayment to the related standard invoice help prevent?
options: Paying the supplier's deposit amount twice
The supplier going out of business
Late payment penalties from the supplier
questions.explain: Without applying the prepayment, the full standard invoice amount could be paid on top of the deposit already sent.
